bibliography.title: Locality-aware Parallel Decoding for Efficient Autoregressive Image Generation

read_scope.notes: The verified proceedings PDF has 24 physical pages and no separate supplementary file.

layout_observations: Main pages use a two-column ICLR layout; p.1 Figure 1 occupies the right column, p.2 Figure 2 spans the page width, and p.8–9 tables span both columns.
Figures 4–5 share the left side of p.4 while their explanatory text occupies the right; Figure 6 is a full-width comparison on p.5.
Appendix pages 17–24 are primarily single-column; p.19 is dominated by code, p.21 by attention maps, p.22–23 by qualitative images, and p.24 leaves a large lower-page white area after Figure 14.

boundary_evidence.anchor: Our contributions lie in two key aspects

abstract_sentences.text: We present Locality-aware Parallel Decoding (LPD) to accelerate autoregressive image generation.
Traditional autoregressive image generation relies on next-patch prediction, a memory-bound process that leads to high latency.

evidence.anchor: a memory-bound process that leads to high latency

abstract_sentences.text: Existing works have tried to parallelize next-patch prediction by shifting to multi-patch prediction to accelerate the process, but only achieved limited parallelization.

To achieve high parallelization while maintaining generation quality, we introduce two key techniques: (1) Flexible Parallelized Autoregressive Modeling, a novel architecture that enables arbitrary generation ordering and degrees of parallelization.
It uses learnable position query tokens to guide generation at target positions while ensuring mutual visibility among concurrently generated tokens for consistent parallel decoding.

evidence.anchor: ensuring mutual visibility among concurrently generated tokens

abstract_sentences.text: (2) Locality-aware Generation Ordering, a novel schedule that forms groups to minimize intra-group dependencies and maximize contextual support, enhancing generation quality.

evidence.anchor: minimize intra-group dependencies and maximize contextual support

abstract_sentences.text: With these designs, we reduce the generation steps from 256 to 20 (256×256 res.) and 1024 to 48 (512×512 res.) without compromising quality on the ImageNet class-conditional generation, and achieving at least 3.4× lower latency than previous parallelized autoregressive models.

method_summary.inputs_outputs: At training, interleaved ground-truth context and target-position queries map each query to its ground-truth token. At inference, generated image tokens update the cache while position queries decode target logits in parallel; Algorithm 1 outputs an ordered list of grid positions.

claim_closure.claim: Flat-token AR one-token decoding creates a memory-bound latency bottleneck.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq. (1), group formulation, position queries, and KV-cache inference address sequential steps.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 1 and Tables 1–3 report steps/latency; Figure 14 profiles batch regimes.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 repeats fewer steps and lower latency.

claim_closure.claim: Flexible Parallelized AR supports arbitrary order/degree while giving same-step queries mutual visibility.
claim_closure.method_response: Position query tokens, Context/Query Attention, fused mask, and generated-token-only cache implement the mechanism.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 9(a) compares low-step FID under random order; Figure 12 shows random-region editing.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 names flexible parallelized autoregressive modeling as a main contribution.

evidence.anchor: ensures mutual visibility among the position query tokens within the same step

claim_closure.claim: Locality-aware order jointly uses proximity to context and repulsion within a group.
claim_closure.method_response: Eq. (3), Algorithm 1, thresholds τ/ρ, and farthest-point sampling operationalize both principles.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 7 supports locality; Figure 9(b/c) and Table 6 test schedule, synergy, and sensitivity.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 names locality-aware generation order as the second contribution.

evidence.anchor: High proximity to previously generated tokens

claim_closure.method_response: Group factorization, dynamic cosine group sizes, flexible architecture, and locality schedule.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Tables 1–2 report matched raster/LPD FID, IS, Precision, Recall, latency, and throughput.

claim_closure.method_response: Gemma text encoder, progressive-resolution training, and the same locality schedule.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Table 3, Table 7, and Figure 13 show GenEval and qualitative examples.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 does not separately recover this extension.

claim_closure.claim: LPD supports zero-shot class editing, inpainting, and outpainting.
claim_closure.method_response: Arbitrary target order, KV prefill for non-repaint regions, and class-embedding substitution.
claim_closure.evidence_response: Figure 12 provides qualitative panels and the operational description.

evidence.anchor: generate the masked region in a random order

claim_closure.claim: Flat representation preserves interoperability with CLIP/DINO-like perception backbones.
claim_closure.method_response: The paper retains flat tokens but presents no downstream perception method.
claim_closure.evidence_response: CLIP/DINO appear in motivation only; no interoperability task or result table is provided.

claim_closure.claim: High-resolution efficiency advantage is broadly deployment-relevant.
claim_closure.method_response: Position queries and KV cache reduce steps; Figure 14 examines batch regime.
claim_closure.evidence_response: A100/BFloat16 profiling shows near-12× memory-bound throughput and approximately 3× maximum-batch advantage, with compute-bound degradation.
claim_closure.conclusion_response: §6 retains a lower-latency claim without restating the regime boundary.

lexical_profile.rhetorical_profile: Strong claims cluster around enables/supports/guarantees/without sacrificing and are usually paired with figures or tables; weaker claims use suggests/indicates/intuitively/approximately for locality, regime transitions, and qualitative extension. The PDF extraction and table/code overlap make the lexical counts approximate.

evidence.anchor: This analysis supports our two principles

final_judgment.single_storyline: LPD decouples context representation from target generation using position queries and same-step mutual visibility, then uses attention-locality-driven proximity/repulsion scheduling to choose parallel groups; ImageNet tables connect the mechanism to step, quality, and latency outcomes.
final_judgment.main_body_keeps: The main text keeps Eq. (1)–(3), the Algorithm 1 proximity line, mask/cache diagrams, Algorithm 1, locality figures, Tables 1–3, Figure 9 ablations, and the §3.3 compute-bound caveat.
final_judgment.appendix_moves: Architecture dimensions, training hyperparameters, text-to-image data, schedule code, τ/ρ sensitivity, extra attention maps, qualitative images, per-category GenEval, and batch-throughput curves move to Appendix A–E.
final_judgment.best_pattern: Figure 7 makes locality observable, Algorithm 1 makes the two principles executable, Figure 9(c) isolates their synergy, and Tables 1–3 translate the mechanism into matched system numbers.
final_judgment.largest_gap: There is no formal guarantee, uncertainty/seed reporting, cross-model locality transfer, quantitative editing evaluation, or interoperability test; parameter counts also conflict between main text and Appendix Table 4.
final_judgment.transfer_rule: For decoding-acceleration claims, pair mechanism-specific diagnostics with matched raster/control comparisons, component or principle ablations, and a batch-regime efficiency profile.
final_judgment.transfer_boundary: The rule applies when memory bandwidth and spatial locality govern token decoding; compute-bound operation, non-local attention, or editing/perception tasks require additional evidence before speed or quality claims can be generalized.
